messages:
maria: heads up — started seeing a spike in quota errors after we flipped default routing to v2 for production traffic. dashboards show increased 429s for some long-tail customers.

sanjay: ugh. noticed it too on the quota-summaries page, looked like v2 requests were counted against v1 reserved pools?

alex: can you paste an example request id / customer id? i want to trace routing

maria:  reqId=8f3a2b, tenant=acme-inc. stack trace shows routed to v2 pool, but quota meter in console displays v1 pool consumption.

julia: probable cause: our quota-aggregation job still uses header X-API-Version to bucket usage, but the routing layer rewrites that to v2-after-fallback. telemetry changed during rollout and mismatch happened.

kevin: timeline: yesterday 04:00 we enabled 'prefer-v2' routing policy with fallthrough to compatible-v1. we didn't update the quota-telemetry shim.

maria: short-term: can we flip routing back to strict v1 for affected orgs while we patch metrics?

alex: yes, we can do per-tenant routing override. ops-bot can run the rollbacks if we tag orgs.

ops-bot: running command: `rbctl route override --tenant acme-inc --version v1 --reason "quota-metric-mismatch"` — queued for approval. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

julia: for the fix: options are (A) change quota-aggregation to use routing-decisions (preferred), (B) add a telemetry shim that maps rewritten version headers back to original client_version, (C) map quotas in routing layer before rewrite. each has tradeoffs.

sanjay: (A) easiest to reason about long-term — aggregating from routing-decisions gives accurate billing. but it's a bigger change to the ETL job.

kevin: (B) is fastest — we can emit an extra tag `client_version` from the router for metrics pipeline. patch router, backfill? no backfill needed for past spikes but we can correct going forward.

maria: product concern: customers see a spike in console quota usage for v1 which is incorrect — they'll open tickets. we should add a banner + incident note in console while we fix.

julia: agreed. propose temporary banner: "Quota metrics for requests routed during the v2 rollout may be misattributed between v1 and v2. We are rolling a fix; data will be accurate within 24h."

alex: also add telemetry event `routing.quota_mismatch` with sample rate 1.0 for first 2 hours so SRE can triage.

kevin: we should also add a rollout-UX improvement: when enabling 'prefer-v2' toggle, warn about quota mapping and offer an auto-simulate check that evaluates possible quota collisions. small modal + doc link.

maria: action items: 1) ops rollback for affected tenants (alex/ops-bot) — in flight. 2) router patch to emit client_version tag (kevin) — target 4h. 3) metrics ETL change tracked as follow-up (julia/sanjay) — target next sprint. 4) console banner + incident note (product/maria). 5) add `routing.quota_mismatch` event (alex).

julia: I'll open a short RFC with diagrams and the telemetry schema change. will include example mapping rules and risk analysis.

sanjay: one more: we need to update our rollout playbook — add a checklist to validate metric parity for at least 24h on canary orgs before full default flip.

maria: thanks. ping me once rollback finishes and when router patch is deployed. :thumbsup:

alex: rollback finished for acme-inc and two other tenants. ops-bot confirms no immediate 429s after. we'll keep watch.

ops-bot: monitor: alert group "quota-errors" 1/5 triggered — trending down.

kevin: starting router patch PR now. i'll cc julia for telemetry schema.

maria: closing loop: we should also add a console tooltip on the routing toggle explaining quota semantics. saves support questions.

julia: noted — adding UX task to RFC.

maria: thanks team. we'll post an incident summary in #incidents after we backfill the initial telemetry and confirm metrics are stable. :white_check_mark:
